Syllabus


Cryo-ET and Subtomogram averaging Workshop






Abstract


The focus of the workshop is to provide training in some of the most recent developments of CryoET and STA data processing using for instance nextPYP, TomoBEAR, Warp/M, taught by the developers themselves. The workshop provides hands-on training in CryoET and STA encompassing all stages of the pipeline.


Keywords: Cryo-electron tomography · Subtomogram averaging · Tomogram reconstruction · Particle picking · Structural biology




Details




Dates


02 Dec 2026 – 04 Dec 2026




Duration


3 days




Delivery


In-person




Location


SciLifeLab Solna




Language


English






Learning outcomes


After completing this training, participants will be able to:



Alignment and reconstruction of tilt series


Manual and automated particle picking


Archiving and cataloguing of tilt series, tomograms and annotations


Creation of subtomogram averaging projects


Advanced tools in subtomogram averaging


Classification methods


Creation of 3D maps





Target audience


PhD students, postdocs and researchers who want to learn cryo-ET data processing and subtomogram averaging


Expertise level: Beginner




Prerequisites




Knowledge



Participants will be selected on the basis of applications that describe their current research projects and plans.


Priority will be given to participants that are currently doing cryoET and are users of the SciLifeLab cryo-EM facilities.





Technical



Participants are required to bring their own laptops with mouse to the workshop.







Forms of instruction and examination




Forms of instruction



Lectures by the software developers


Hands-on data processing tutorials


Discussion and Q&A sessions with the developers





Forms of examination


none






Administration




Organising organisation(s)



SciLifeLab



Content provider(s)



CryoNet


Stockholm University

Preparation


Prepare for the training


The practical sessions run on the SciLifeLab cryo-EM cluster. You use your own laptop to log in to the cluster and to look at the results. Please install the programs below before the course.







Questions about the training?


Get in touch with the training team.

karin.wallden@scilifelab.se








Before the course





Windows: install MobaXterm. macOS and Linux: nothing to install for the cluster.


Install ChimeraX 1.12 with ArtiaX and check that ArtiaX starts.


Install 3dmod and open the test file golgi.mrc.


Bring your laptop and its charger.







Accounts






Cluster account





You work in groups. Each group gets an account on the cluster.




Instructions


You get the user name and password at the start of the course. You do not need to create an account before.








Software requirements






Cluster access





One program for logging in to the cluster and for copying files to your laptop.




Instructions


macOS and Linux: nothing to install. Use the Terminal: ssh to log in, scp to copy files.


Windows: install MobaXterm (free Home Edition). It logs in with SSH and shows the cluster's files in a sidebar, where you can download them.




MobaXterm (Home Edition) download


Step-by-step guide with screenshots








ChimeraX with ArtiaX





To look at tomograms, membranes and particle picks in 3D.




Instructions



Install ChimeraX 1.12.


Install the ArtiaX plugin from the ChimeraX Toolshed.





ChimeraX download


Step-by-step guide with screenshots








3dmod (from IMOD)





To look at tilt series, tomograms and particle picks. Version 5.x.




Instructions


Windows: the standalone 3dmod is enough. macOS and Linux: install IMOD 5.x. See the step-by-step guide.




3dmod for Windows


IMOD for macOS and Linux


Step-by-step guide with screenshots







 Problems with the installation?



Contact Gerrit Timpert (gerrit.timpert@scilifelab.se). If needed, we can also solve it together in a short Zoom call before the course.






Hardware requirements





Laptop





Bring your own laptop (Windows, macOS or Linux) on which you can install software. All computing runs on the cluster.

title: Laptop setup guide
text:
Cryo-ET and Subtomogram averaging Workshop




Overview Content Schedule


Information


Preparation Laptop setup guide Practicalities Announcements Team Syllabus






 





Laptop setup guide
Please install the following programs on your laptop before the course:

a program to log in to the cluster and copy files (Windows only, see below)
ChimeraX 1.12 with the ArtiaX plugin
3dmod, the viewer from IMOD

You need a laptop on which you can install software. Choose your operating system below.






Problems with the installation?



Contact Gerrit Timpert at gerrit.timpert@scilifelab.se. If needed, we can also solve it together in a short Zoom call before the course.



WindowsmacOSLinux (Ubuntu)



1. MobaXterm (cluster login and files)
MobaXterm logs in to the cluster and shows the cluster’s files in a sidebar, where you can download them. The free Home Edition is enough.

Open the MobaXterm download page and click Download now under Home Edition.

Click Installer edition.

Unzip the downloaded file and run the installer in it with the default settings.
Start MobaXterm and click Session.

Click SSH.

Enter login.cryoem.se as Remote host and your course user name as Username. Click OK.

The first time you connect, MobaXterm asks whether you trust the server. Click Accept.

Type your password and press Enter. The password is not shown while you type.

After the login, the sidebar on the left shows your files on the cluster. To copy a file to your laptop, right-click it and choose Download.


MobaXterm saves the session in the sidebar. Next time, double-click it to log in again.


2. ChimeraX 1.12 with ArtiaX

Open the ChimeraX download page. Under the heading ChimeraX 1.12, click ChimeraX-1.12.exe. Do not take the release candidate or the daily build at the top of the page: ArtiaX does not work with them.

Run the installer with the default settings.
Start ChimeraX. Click into the field next to Command: at the bottom of the window, type toolshed install ArtiaX and press Enter. The log shows “Installed ChimeraX-ArtiaX”. If orange warnings about numpy appear above it, you can ignore them.

In the same field, type pip install pandas==3.0.5 and press Enter. The log shows no message for this command. That is normal.







Why this step?



The current ArtiaX release installs a pandas version that does not work with ChimeraX 1.12, so ArtiaX does not start. This step installs a version that works.


Quit ChimeraX (File, Quit) and start it again.
Click the ArtiaX tab at the top, then Launch.

The ArtiaX panel opens. ChimeraX and ArtiaX are ready.




3. 3dmod






Already have IMOD?



If the full IMOD is already installed on your laptop, the standalone 3dmod does not start. Use the 3dmod from your IMOD installation and skip this part.


On Windows you only need 3dmod, not the full IMOD. 3dmod is available as a standalone package.

Open the 3dmod download folder and click 3dmodForWin64-5.2.7.exe.

Double-click the downloaded file. Keep the destination folder C:\Program Files and click Extract.

If Windows shows a blue warning, click More info and then Run anyway. If Windows asks for administrator rights, right-click the file and choose Run as administrator.
Open the folder C:\Program Files\3dmod.

Right-click 3dmod and choose Send to, Desktop (create shortcut). On Windows 11, you may first have to click Show more options.

Start 3dmod from the desktop shortcut. In the window “3dmod Startup”, click Select… next to Image file(s), choose a file and click OK.

To test it, download golgi.mrc and open it. 3dmod shows the image, and its info window shows “3dmod 5.2.7”.





The screenshots show a Mac with Apple Silicon (M1, M2, …).

1. Cluster login and files
Nothing to install. Open the app Terminal (in Applications, Utilities).

To log in, type the following and press Enter. Use your course user name instead of <user>.
ssh <user>@login.cryoem.se

The first time you connect, the Terminal asks whether you want to continue connecting. Type yes and press Enter. Then type your password and press Enter. The password is not shown while you type. After the login, the prompt shows your user name and login1.

To log out, type exit. To copy a file from the cluster to your laptop, use scp in a Terminal on your laptop (not on the cluster):
scp <user>@login.cryoem.se:<path on the cluster> ~/Downloads/



2. IMOD (3dmod)
IMOD needs Python on the Mac.

In the Terminal, type python3 --version and press Enter. If it shows a version number, Python is installed and you can go on with step 2.

If it shows an error or asks to install developer tools, install Python first: the IMOD download page links the Python 3.10 installer from python.org in its Mac section.
Open the IMOD download page and go to Latest Stable Release Packages - Mac. For a Mac with Apple Silicon, click clickable installer in the line Mac OS 12 - 27 for arm64 processor. For an Intel Mac, use the line for Intel processor.

Double-click the downloaded .pkg file and follow the installer with the default settings. It asks for your Mac password.

Close the Terminal and open a new one. The new Terminal knows where IMOD is. Type which 3dmod: it shows /Applications/IMOD/bin/3dmod.

Type 3dmod and press Enter. In the window “3dmod Startup”, click Select… next to Image file(s), choose a file and click OK. Do not use the 3dmod icon in Launchpad: it does not work.

To test it, download golgi.mrc and open it. 3dmod shows the image.




3. ChimeraX 1.12 with ArtiaX

Open the ChimeraX download page. Under the heading ChimeraX 1.12, click ChimeraX-1.12.dmg. For an Intel Mac, click Other platforms below it. Do not take the release candidate or the daily build: ArtiaX does not work with them.

Open the .dmg file and drag ChimeraX-1.12 to Applications.

Start ChimeraX from Applications. The first start shows a registration form. You can fill it in or close it.

Click into the field next to Command: at the bottom of the window, type toolshed install ArtiaX and press Enter. The log shows “Installed ChimeraX-ArtiaX”. Orange warnings about numpy above it are normal and can be ignored.

In the same field, type pip install pandas==3.0.5 and press Enter. The log shows no message for this command. That is normal.







Why this step?



The current ArtiaX release installs a pandas version that does not work with ChimeraX 1.12, so ArtiaX does not start. This step installs a version that works.


Quit ChimeraX (ChimeraX, Quit ChimeraX) and start it again.
Click the ArtiaX tab at the top, then Launch.

The ArtiaX panel opens. ChimeraX and ArtiaX are ready.





These instructions are for Ubuntu 22.04 and 24.04.

1. Cluster login and files
Nothing to install. In a terminal, use ssh to log in and scp to copy files:
ssh <user>@login.cryoem.se
scp <user>@login.cryoem.se:<path on the cluster> .


2. ChimeraX 1.12 with ArtiaX

Open the ChimeraX download page. Under the heading ChimeraX 1.12, click Other platforms and download ucsf-chimerax_1.12ubuntu24.04_amd64.deb (Ubuntu 24.04) or ucsf-chimerax_1.12ubuntu22.04_amd64.deb (Ubuntu 22.04).
Install it, for example on Ubuntu 24.04:
sudo apt install ~/Downloads/ucsf-chimerax_1.12ubuntu24.04_amd64.deb
Start ChimeraX with the command chimerax.
Follow steps 3 to 7 of the Windows instructions: toolshed install ArtiaX, then pip install pandas==3.0.5, restart ChimeraX, then ArtiaX, Launch.



3. IMOD (3dmod)

Open the IMOD download page and download the package under Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8 - CUDA 12 (imod_5.1.13_RHEL8-64_CUDA12.0.sh). Despite its name, this is the package the IMOD team recommends for Ubuntu 20 and newer.
Install it from a terminal in the download folder:
sudo sh imod_5.1.13_RHEL8-64_CUDA12.0.sh
Log out and log in again, then open a terminal and type 3dmod. See the Windows instructions, step 5, for how to open a file.
